title: Included excursions are not free excursions
subtitle: They are in the fare. What matters is whether they're the ones you'd choose.

text: A daily included tour is convenience, not curation.
sub: River fares usually cover one guided excursion a day, a good local guide and the coach. Excellent value, genuinely — but built for a hundred people at once, not for you.

left.label: Included
items: One tour a day, in the fare

right.label: Curated
items: A car and a private guide

title: Three days I'd pay to upgrade

items.head: A Douro wine morning
items.body: A private table at a quinta beats a group tasting on a timetable. The one I argue for most.

items.head: A town you already know
items.body: If you have walked Melk before, the included walk is a wasted morning. Go somewhere else.

items.head: Anything you actually love
items.body: Gardens, presses, cathedral organs. Specialist interest is what a group tour cannot serve.

quote: Included means someone chose for you. That's a service on five days and a waste on two.

text: Take the included tour on days you have no strong opinion.
sub: Then spend on the two or three where you do. That mix costs far less than moving up a fare grade, and it gives you a better week than either extreme.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Or send me the itinerary and I'll mark the days worth upgrading and the ones that are fine as sold.
